# ZenoFCIS

ZenoFCIS is a Rust library family for high-assurance functional-core /
imperative-shell systems.

Current workspace version: 1.0.0-rc.1
Current status: first public API and packaging candidate; final Cargo V1
stability and general deployment qualification are not yet claimed
Rust toolchain: 1.97.1 for repository validation

## Start here

- docs/INSTALLATION.md: exact dependency and source installation
- docs/QUICKSTART.md: supported project adoption path
- docs/API_REFERENCE.md: public API entry points and rustdoc
- docs/CRATE_MAP.md: crate roles and trust boundaries
- docs/FEATURE_MATRIX.md: umbrella features and environments
- docs/LLM_USAGE.md: authority rules for model-assisted work
- docs/ARCHITECTURE.md: dependency rings
- docs/RC1_RELEASE_NOTES.md: candidate surface and final-release blockers
- docs/V1_RELEASE_CHECKLIST.md: exact-source tag, publication, evidence, and rollback runbook
- docs/PACKAGING.md: package authority and retained artifacts
- docs/RELEASE_ASSURANCE.md: repository gates and nonclaims

## Safe golden path

ProjectProfile + ProjectCatalog
-> generated typed transition or typed DomainMachine implementations
-> ComposedDomainProgram for multi-domain projects
-> complete project LawManifest and verified law evidence
-> CatalogCommitAuthority::execute
-> private CatalogAuthorizedTransition
-> AuthorizedShellState or policy-pinned concrete shell

The authority owns the catalog, program, law engine, provider, interpreter,
deployment, replay policy, and limits. Request callers supply admitted
invocation values, not prebuilt decisions or bundles.

## Important public APIs

- project: ProjectProfile, RegistryEntry, ProfileEvolution
- schema/catalog: Schema, ProjectCatalog, CatalogLimits
- transition: CataloguedTransitionBuilder, TransitionDecision
- composition: CompositionSpec, ComponentContract, Footprint
- domain execution: DomainMachine, MachineInterface, ExecutableComposition
- composed program: ComposedDomainProgram, ProjectionPlan
- laws: LawManifest, ProjectLawEngine, verify_project_laws
- authority: CatalogCommitAuthority, InvocationWitness,
  CatalogAuthorizedTransition
- formal tools: BackendEngine, BackendVerifier, EvidenceChecker,
  LawEvidenceVerifier
- shells: AuthorizedShellState; zeno-fcis-shell-sqlite when enabled

## Production integration rules

- Do not use CommitBundle, TransitionDecision, or NormalizedDecision as commit
  authority.
- Do not use apply_reference_bundle as a production commit port.
- Do not let a caller choose schemas, stable IDs, precedence, laws, providers,
  verifiers, interpreters, deployments, or promotion status.
- Keep clocks, randomness, filesystems, networks, databases, threads, async
  runtimes, mutable globals, and executable effect closures outside the core.
- Ordinary Reject has no candidate, state change, effect, or outbox obligation.
- CommittedFailure explicitly binds any intentional authoritative change.
- Bind evidence to exact source, profile, schema, algorithm, assumptions,
  artifact, coverage, toolchain, and independent verifier.

## Formal tools

The backend and evidence protocols are tool neutral. Public users may mount
Lean, SMT/Z3, CVC5, Kani, Flux, or another checker. Private ESSO users may
implement the same traits in a private crate. Missing tools, timeouts, crashes,
unknown results, and checker disagreement grant no authority.

## Deterministic parallelism

The library contains proof-carrying composition, footprint/conflict analysis,
commutativity evidence, and sequential-versus-composed parity surfaces.
Canonical sequential execution is the normative runtime oracle.

Nonclaim: no concurrent scheduler, threaded shell, or production parallel
runtime is currently shipped. Production parallel promotion also requires
complete static footprint witnesses and checked equality with the canonical
sequential result.

## Project-specific and reference surfaces

- zeno-fcis-profile-zenodex and zeno-fcis-adapter-zenodex are project-specific.
- zeno-fcis-shell is pure reference semantics.
- authenticated-state and persistent collection implementations are reference
  or optimization surfaces unless separately qualified. The
  `authenticated-authority` feature adds retained-evidence projector
  qualification, exact candidate binding, strict persisted-plan
  reauthorization, and a nominal production-facing publication port. It does
  not turn the bounded reference tree into a production datastore.
- code generation synchronizes reviewed definitions; it does not prove them.

## Validation commands

python3 tools/check_assurance.py --self-test
cargo +1.97.1 fmt --all -- --check
cargo +1.97.1 clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings
cargo +1.97.1 test --workspace --all-features --locked
cargo +1.97.1 test --workspace --doc --all-features --locked
RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo +1.97.1 doc --workspace --all-features --locked --no-deps

Do not report exact-head green unless permanent read-only workflows passed at
that exact commit.
